newsitem.title: UK: Rating agencies give BT thumbs down, MCI thumbs up.
newsitem.headline: Rating agencies give BT thumbs down, MCI thumbs up.

text.p: International credit rating agencies said on Monday they may cut British Telecommunications Plc's star rating because its planned 20 billion pound ($32.75 billion) merger with MCI Communications Corp would crank up debt levels.
MCI is likely to get a boost to its ratings, although a full analysis of the credit implications of the proposed merger needed to be carried out, the agencies said.

Both Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's said they would review the merger deal announced on Sunday. BT offered a mixture of cash and shares to boost its stake in MCI to 100 percent from 20 percent and create a telecommunications giant called Concert Plc.

"The review of BT's ratings was prompted by the announcement that BT and MCI have entered into a merger agreement to create a global telecommunications company which will have a stronger competitive position but significantly higher debt leverage," Moody's Investor Service said in a statement.

S&P said: "Though Concert's financial profile on a pro-forma basis is expected to remain strong following the merger, the group will face significant capital investment needs and a higher industry risk than BT is currently exposed to."
Moody's said it had placed its AAA senior debt rating for BT and its guaranteed subsidiaries under review for possible downgrade. The short-term Prime 1 rating of BT is unaffected, it said.
Standard & Poor's said its AAA senior unsecured debt rating of BT and related entities was put on CreditWatch with negative implications -- meaning the rating could be cut.

Meanwhile, Moody's said it confirmed the A2 senior, A3 subordinated long-term, and Prime 1 short-term debt ratings of MCI. S&P said MCI's A long-term and A1 short-term ratings were put on CreditWatch with positive implications.
"Moody's review will focus on whether the funding of this transaction will affect BT's future ability to sustain its very strong debt protection ratios," Moody's said.
It said it would also review the potential for additional investment needs to develop a more aggressive international strategy at a time when competitive pressure is expected to increase in Britain.
Moody's said it would analyse the operational and strategic benefits, as well as integration risk to result from the merger.
"The proposed transaction could strategically reinforce the positions of both entities," it said.

"It could also leverage the strengths of both MCI and BT, to take full advantage of the opportunities emerging from the liberalisation processes in both America and European telecommunications markets." ($1=.6107 Pound)
